items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Personnel -- Marshall Royal, Harry Carney, Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Tricky Sam Nanton, Juan Tizol... Do you remember making a short subject with Florence Mills and Bessie Dudley? For Paramount?

ctx.x: they laugh at jokes that don't mean anything. And the same thing at that time, too.

There is also a listing here for "Bundle of Blues," 1938. It was "an eight minute short; a Paramount musical short featuring Duke Ellington and his orchestra with 'Rocking and Rhythm,' a vocal rendering of 'Stormy Weather' by Ivy Anderson and a tap dance routine from Florence Mills and Bessie Dudley to 'Bugle Call Rag.'" "Personnel -- Marshall Royal, Harry Carney, Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Tricky Sam Nanton, Juan Tizol, Lawrence Brown, trombones; Cootie Williams, Arthur Whetsol, Freddie Jenkins, trumpets;…
Do you remember making a short subject with Florence Mills and Bessie Dudley? For Paramount?

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: His name didn't get in the listing. Marshal Royal, whose name doesn't get into the listing.

ctx.x: In his book, "Jazz In the Movies", by David Meeker, they have a listing of Belle of the Nineties and there is a picture from it, and you're in the picture; I guess it was probably taken on the set, and it said it was at Paramount Studios in 1934. And it says it's one of the classic Mae West vehicles in which she portrays a tough 19th Century showgirl in love with a young boxer. Duke Ellington was all and sometimes part of his orchestra, provides the backing off and on screen for the songs, When A St. Louis Woman…
Uh huh. That was his name -- the saxophone player with Count Basie. His name didn't get in the listing. Marshal Royal, whose name doesn't get into the listing.
He was what? Instead of Toby?
